# The historical EWS create listener reports remote success before header persistence and final status

The renamed listener receives remote-created ID and returns a local header, then Rust parses original MIME content, populates it and calls onHdrPopulated so the C++ commitHeader closure persists it. The key callback follows, and outer OnStopCreate reports the inner result. Thus remote success is not complete local-copy success and later parsing/persistence errors remain possible. Part 4 moves listener argument first consistently across IDL/C++/Rust. Current listener later reports only remote-finished status/ID; retired signatures are historical examples, not current recipes. No create/copy or test ran.

Scope: EWS Part4 message-create callback phases.
